Creality took full advantage of its appearance at RAPID + TCT 2026 in Boston this week to present its broad hardware and software portfolio spanning 3D printing, 3D scanning, laser processing, filament recycling, and cloud-based management.
Creality took full advantage of its appearance at RAPID + TCT 2026 in Boston this week to present its broad hardware and software portfolio spanning 3D printing, 3D scanning, laser processing, filament recycling, and cloud-based management. The company’s end-to-end workflow line-up, which connects each stage of the manufacturing process from physical object capture through to finished part production, was in full demo mode as it gave the North American market a hands-on opportunity to see its range – including recent launches – up close.
Creality also presented the Filament Maker M1 and Shredder R1, launched on Indiegogo earlier this month, and which it claims is the first integrated desktop system designed to recycle waste plastic and produce custom filament. The crowdfunding campaign for the product has to date raised just under HK$45 million ( $5.7m).
Creality also highlighted the addition of MagicRelief to its cloud platform.
